title: India Tells Its Nationals in Saudi Arabia: Stay Indoors During Aerial Attacks
excerpt: The Embassy of India in Riyadh updated its advisory on October 15: stay indoors during aerial attacks, do not film interceptions, and note that Indian-carrier suspensions are stretching to October 24.
body:
• The Embassy of India in Riyadh updated its advisory at 5 p.m. on October 15: Indians in Saudi Arabia should keep following local authorities and stay indoors in case of an aerial attack.
  • New warning: filming or sharing information about missile/drone interceptions and impact sites can bring legal liability under Saudi law.
  • Embassy helplines (from the current advisory series): toll-free 8002471234, WhatsApp +966-536216082 (Riyadh) and +966-536209704 (Jeddah consulate).
  • Flights: Riyadh airport operations remain suspended; Indian carriers are halted until October 17, with Akasa extending Riyadh to October 24 and IndiGo to October 24.

India's embassy in Riyadh issued an updated advisory for Indians in Saudi Arabia at 5 p.m. on October 15, telling nationals to continue following local authorities and to stay indoors in case of an aerial attack, NDTV reported. The update, posted by the embassy as @IndianEmbRiyadh, is expressly in continuation of its previous advisories during this month's Houthi attacks on Saudi civilian infrastructure.

The fresh element is legal. The advisory warns that filming, publishing or sharing information related to countering missiles and drones — and to their impact sites — exposes the individual to legal liability under local rules. It also tells nationals who need to leave urgently that they may consider flights from neighbouring Bahrain, Kuwait and Qatar, obtaining the necessary entry visas themselves, and warns travellers to Saudi Arabia, including Umrah pilgrims, to expect short-notice flight disruptions.

The Helplines to Save

The embassy's current advisory series lists a toll-free number within Saudi Arabia, 8002471234, a WhatsApp line (messages only) at +966-536216082, and phone numbers +966-554412016 and +966-542126784. The Consulate General in Jeddah can be reached at +966-12-2614093 and +966-556122301, with WhatsApp at +966-536209704. A new control room has also been set up at the Indian Haj Pilgrims Office in Makkah, alongside the existing 24-hour Jeddah control room, to assist stranded passengers.

The Injured from October 10

The update also carried news of the Indians hurt in the October 10 attack on Riyadh's airport, in which one Indian national was killed and 11 injured. Several of the injured remain in hospital — two in intensive care — and one more was discharged on Thursday, the embassy said. Ambassador Vipul, in a separate video message on October 15 reported by IANS, condemned the attacks on civilian facilities, expressed condolences to the victims' families, and urged the community to remain calm and alert.

Flights: Suspensions Are Lengthening

King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remains suspended, while Dammam, Jeddah and Medina operate with some disruptions. Indian carriers — Air India, Air India Express, Akasa Air and IndiGo — are suspended to and from Saudi Arabia until October 17, and the extensions have already begun: Akasa has pushed its Riyadh suspension to October 24 and Jeddah to October 21, and IndiGo has extended Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Medina to October 24, NDTV reported. Saudi carriers Saudia and Flynas continue limited services. The background for travellers is our earlier coverage of cancellations through October 17 and the 24-hour control room for Umrah pilgrims.

An estimated 2.4–2.7 million Indians live and work in Saudi Arabia. The embassy's advice to them is unchanged in substance and sharper in one respect: stay indoors during an attack — and keep your phone camera down while it happens.
nri_angle: Directly actionable for the Gulf’s largest Indian community: the embassy’s helpline numbers and stay-indoors guidance are in the takeaways.
